issuing_body: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, State Demonstrations Group
title: Minnesota SUD Program Integrity Approval Letter and Approved Program Integrity Plan
supports: CMS approved Minnesota's Program Integrity Plan for the Minnesota Substance Use Disorder System Reform section 1115(a) demonstration on 2026-08-04, finding it consistent with STC 3.16.
The current demonstration period runs through 2031-03-31; the approved plan states the extension period is 2026-04-01 through 2031-03-31.

CMS states the program-integrity obligation includes provider screening and enrollment, pre- and post-payment review, payment methodologies and rate setting, utilization controls, identifying/investigating/referring suspected fraud, complaint intake, and safeguards against fraud, waste and abuse.
The Minnesota plan states that its program-integrity measures are not limited to the SUD waiver population and align with Minnesota's broader CMS corrective-action work.

The plan records January 2026 pre-payment review for high-risk services, provider revalidation, inactive-provider terminations, enhanced analytics, post-payment review, law-enforcement referrals, program assessments, and additional controls.

The plan states that Minnesota Medicaid managed-care plans serve more than 80 percent of approximately 1.2 million Medicaid enrollees and that the Legislature appropriated funds for additional managed-care post-payment review.
The plan states that current analytics are rules-based and descriptive and do not include automated decision-making or machine-learning models.
important_qualifications: CMS approval of the plan is approval of a compliance/oversight framework, not a finding that every listed vulnerability or suspicious claim is fraud.
Agency-reported counts and recovery figures embedded in the state plan retain AGENCY_POSITION status unless independently audited or adjudicated.

The plan's reference to CMS approval of Minnesota's broader corrective action plan on 2026-03-19 is evidence within a CMS-approved federal record, but the standalone March 19 approval letter should still be captured if available.
